The query and document embeddings are L2 normalized in the methods [`query`](colbert/modeling/colbert.py#L155) and [`doc`](colbert/modeling/colbert.py#L165) so that their dot product (in functions like [`colbert_score`](colbert/modeling/colbert.py#L205)) becomes the cosine similarity.

````python

def forward(self, Q, D):
        Q = self.query(*Q)
        D, D_mask = self.doc(*D, keep_dims='return_mask')

        print(f"Q shape: {Q.shape}")
        print(f"D shape: {D.shape}")

        # Save only the last epoch tensors Q and D:
        torch.save(Q, 'all_query_embeddings.pt')
        torch.save(D, 'all_document_embeddings.pt')
        print("Last Q and D saved.")

        # Repeat each query encoding for every corresponding document.
        Q_duplicated = Q.repeat_interleave(self.colbert_config.nway, dim=0).contiguous()
        scores = self.score(Q_duplicated, D, D_mask)

        if self.colbert_config.use_ib_negatives:
            ib_loss = self.compute_ib_loss(Q, D, D_mask)
            return scores, ib_loss

        return scores
````

This way, every call to forward will simply write out the current Q and D so that when you reach the last epoch only the most recent embeddings are saved.

      epoch_Q = torch.cat(epoch_query_embeddings, dim=0)

      torch.save(epoch_Q, f'epoch_{epoch}_all_query_embeddings.pt')
